item.title: Kitten Found Alone Outside at a Month Old Can Go From Lap-Melting Cuddles to Full Chaos in a Minute
item.description:
A long-haired grey kitten was found all alone outside when he was barely a month old, and a year later, he has grown into a cat who can go from lap-melting cuddles to full-speed chaos in the space of a single minute.

GreysonCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

This week, Greyson had a birthday. He turned one year old on September 22, a milestone that once looked a long way off.

He arrived at Pet Haven Minnesota last October as a tiny orphan, found outside on his own with no mother or littermates nearby. He was small enough to need round-the-clock bottle feeding, and a foster volunteer named Kris stepped in to give him exactly what was required.

That was nearly a year ago. Greyson has spent every day since in foster care, now with a foster named Jada, and he is still looking for the family who gets to keep him.

Greyson as the palm-sized bottle baby LoveMeow first metCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

When LoveMeow first shared his story, Greyson was a palm-sized bundle of gray fluff with a very big voice. He cried loudly for his meals and made his opinions known long before he could walk in a straight line.

Feeding him was not straightforward. He could only take small amounts at a time and did better sitting upright, so Kris fed him often and carefully, one small meal after another, until the weight began to come.

Barely bigger than the hand that fed him, and already all fluffCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

He was a fighter from the beginning. Greyson met every hurdle in front of him and kept growing fluffier and stronger, purring through all of it as though the hard parts belonged to someone else.

Early on, his fosters learned he had been born with a condition called congenital megacolon. A veterinary technician foster named Abby led the effort to manage it, and after a series of medication and diet trials, they found the routine that keeps him well.

Growing up in foster care, one scratcher box at a timeCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

Today that routine is a small, easy part of his day, and the rescue is proud of how well he does with it. "He takes everything like a champ; it's very easy, and his personality outweighs any medical needs," Eleanor, the marketing coordinator at Pet Haven Minnesota, told LoveMeow.

His condition, in other words, is close to the least interesting thing about him. Kris, the volunteer who bottle-raised him, sums Greyson up as "an energetic mix of playful yet cuddly," and that blend is the first thing most people notice.

Greyson at the wheel of his cardboard getaway truckCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

Eleanor puts it another way, describing him as "a little Jekyll and Hyde, which is amazing." One version of Greyson is pure motion, a gray streak who dives through tunnels and treats a cardboard truck like a getaway car.

He carries the full engine of a one-year-old cat and sees no reason to hide it. Toys go flying, tunnels get conquered, and anyone willing to join the game becomes his favorite person for the afternoon.

The tornado winding down, whiskers and allCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

Then, with very little warning, the other Greyson arrives. The switch tends to flip first thing in the morning, or the moment he spots someone he loves.

The cat who was a gray streak a minute ago melts into the nearest lap. "He runs to you. He's purring. He wants a million headbutts, a million pets," Eleanor said.

Settled into a favorite spotCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

That purr is his signature. Kris credits Greyson with "an excellent (and loud) purr motor that runs non-stop," and he leans into every scratch like he has been saving it up all day.

In Jada's home now, he is in no hurry about any of it. "If he can sit on your lap, he will just roll around for 10 minutes straight," Eleanor said. Greyson does not do much halfway, and affection is no exception.

A full year older, surveying the room he has grown up inCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

For all that charm, a full year has gone by, and Greyson is still in foster care. Greyson has grown up, filled out, learned the house, and met every visitor with the same open heart, but the right person hasn't walked in yet.

Pet Haven continues to advocate for the greatest care for him. Greyson, for his part, looks entirely ready, as certain of a warm welcome as he has ever been.

AdorableCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

A year ago, Greyson was a hand-fed orphan who fit in one palm and was not promised an easy road. Today he is a healthy, handsome, one-year-old cat with two personalities and a lifetime of headbutts saved up for whoever finally gets to keep him.

Turning one means something different for a kitten who started as small as Greyson did.

Happy Birthday Greyson! Credit: Jada Kitten Foster

Share this story with your friends. View more on Greyson and Pet Haven Minnesota on Instagram @pethavenmn and Facebook or pethavenmn.org. Follow along with his current foster, Jada, at @jadakittenfoster, and see where his journey began with Kris at @campwobblycat and Abby at @abbysfostercatchaos.

item.title: Two Kittens Thrown From a Moving Truck Soaked in Bleach Held On to Each Other Until Help Arrived
item.description:
Two young kittens named Dolly and Monroe were thrown from a moving car inside a duffel bag, and a few weeks later, the two of them have come back stronger, healthier, and refusing to be apart.

Dolly and MonroeCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

It began on Manchester Road in St. Louis, with a moment that would have been easy to miss. A woman driving by noticed a duffel bag flying out of the window of a moving pickup truck. Something about it felt wrong to her, and instead of continuing, she pulled over to look.

Inside the bag were two kittens, each only about five and a half months old, both soaked in what appeared to be bleach. She gathered them up and drove straight to the Humane Society of Missouri's headquarters on Macklind Avenue. The veterinary team met her at the door and got to work, washing the chemical from their fur and checking every inch for harm.

The kittens were thin, frightened, and worn down by whatever had led them into that bag. What they were not, for the first time, was alone.

Monroe, still damp from her first bath, the day she arrived at the shelterCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

One of the first photos taken of Monroe shows her still damp from that initial bath, her white coat clinging to a frame far too small, her eyes wide and unsure. The volunteers examined both kittens carefully for any damage to their skin, their eyes, and their ears.

Over the days that followed, the veterinarians kept the two girls close, watching for any lasting effects and running tests that would ensure the kittens were truly in the clear. The news, when it came, was good. "This is an incredibly disturbing act of cruelty, but it is also a powerful example of how one person's decision to stop and help can save a life," Kathy Warnick of the Humane Society of Missouri shared with LoveMeow.

Dolly, bright-eyed and curious, stopping to see what everyone is doingCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

Dolly recovered like a cat with somewhere to be. She is the one with the small black cap set high on her white head, the one who walks right up to see what you are doing and tips her chin for a better look.

A few short weeks made all the difference. The kitten who had arrived underweight and afraid grew rounder, brighter, and bolder, until the fear of that first day had nowhere left to sit.

Dolly settled in as though she has always lived hereCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

These days Dolly stretches out along the back of a chair as though she has always owned it, one paw folded neatly beneath her chest. She settles in wherever she pleases and dares anyone to suggest otherwise.

Wherever Dolly goes, Monroe is not far behind. The two of them are rarely found in separate corners of a room, and where one of them lands, the other tends to appear a moment later.

Monroe watching the roomCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

Monroe is the quieter study of the two, with a bold patch of black drawn over one eye and ear like a mask she was born wearing. She watches a room before she joins it, then folds herself down beside her companion and lets the world come to her.

None of it would have been possible without the stranger who trusted her own instincts on Manchester Road. "Because she acted, these two kittens are safe, receiving medical care and have the opportunity for the happy lives they deserve," Warnick shared.

Two of them rarely far apartCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

You can see what they mean to each other in the smallest moments. Dolly leans in to groom the top of Monroe's head, and Monroe closes her eyes and lets her, the two of them pressed close on a shared blanket as though the rest of the room has fallen away.

Both girls have since been spayed and cleared by the veterinary team, and they are now looking for a home together. Whoever takes one of these girls will certainly be taking both, because they've made it clear they come as a set.

Monroe today, healthy and settledCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

Not long ago, Dolly and Monroe were tossed from a moving car and left on the side of the road with nothing. Today they are healthy, inseparable, and entirely themselves, two kittens who decided their story was only getting started.

Share this story with your friends. More on Dolly and Monroe and the Humane Society of Missouri on Instagram @hsmopets and Facebook, or directly at hsmo.org.

item.title: Cat Left Outside a Shelter Leans Into Every Hand as If No One Ever Let Her Down
item.description:
Someone left a cat outside an animal shelter one afternoon. This young cat was left alone with no idea what had happened to her. Now she greets nearly everyone who passes the same way, tipping her head into their hand before they have even reached her.

PixelCredit: AMA Animal Rescue

A cat arrived without warning and with no one to speak for her. One afternoon, she was left outside the shelter building on her own, frightened and unsure of what had happened to the life she knew. No one could say where she had come from or why she had been left behind.

The team at AMA Animal Rescue, a shelter in Brooklyn, New York, took her in right away. They gave her a quiet space, a soft place to rest, and the steady rhythm of people coming and going with food and gentle words. Whatever had brought her to that sidewalk, she was safe now. By every expectation, a cat left that way might have turned fearful or guarded. Pixel, newly named, did the opposite.

Her corner of the shelterCredit: AMA Animal Rescue

From her very first days at the shelter, she stayed soft and open, pressing into the first hands that reached in to help and settling quickly, more interested in the attention than wary of it.

In the weeks since, Pixel has settled into shelter life and made the most of the company around her. She soaks up the attention of the staff and volunteers who stop by her space, treating each visit as a fresh chance for a little more closeness. Some cats shrink from the bustle of a shelter; Pixel leans toward it, perking up at the sound of footsteps and the promise of a visitor.

Right at homeCredit: AMA Animal Rescue

Everyone first notices how much she enjoys people. The caregivers know her greeting by heart now: reach toward her and she meets the hand halfway, pressing her head into it before it has quite arrived, then folding herself in beside whoever will sit with her. "She enjoys attention, loves being petted, and is happiest when she's spending time with her favorite people," AMA Animal Rescue shared with LoveMeow.

Pixel being sweet Credit: AMA Animal Rescue

Whether she is stretched out beside someone or nudging a hand for one more pat, Pixel is at her happiest in company. Set her on a lap, and she stays, content to be wherever her person is. She has a warm, unhurried way about her that makes her difficult to walk past without stopping.

Her looks do not hurt, either. Pixel is a classic tortoiseshell, her coat a patchwork of black, ginger, and gold that catches the light a little differently from every angle.

Ready for a little moreCredit: AMA Animal Rescue

It is hard to look at her without being looked back at. Those wide green eyes follow the movement in the room, and when they settle on a person, they tend to stay, watching to see whether some company might be on its way.

She may not need to be an only cat, either. Staff has watched her take the other shelter cats in stride, studying them calmly rather than bristling. "She has had several positive interactions when seeing other cats, suggesting she could enjoy a feline companion with a proper introduction," the rescue shared.

Sizing up a visitorCredit: AMA Animal Rescue

Nothing is demanding or dramatic about her, the kind of cat who settles into a room and lets the day come to her.

For all her sweetness, Pixel remains at the shelter. Weeks have gone by, and the right person has not yet come for her. "We truly don't understand how this beautiful girl is still waiting," the rescue shared.

Keeping an eye on the neighborsCredit: AMA Animal Rescue

By now she is one of the most settled cats in the building, as comfortable with the daily routines as any cat who has lived in a home for years.

Through it all, Pixel never stopped being gentle, trusting, and glad for company. The right person has not found her yet. When they do, they will meet a cat who has been ready the whole time, waiting with her head tipped up for a hand.

Caught mid-blep Credit: AMA Animal Rescue

Share this story with your friends. Pixel is available for adoption through AMA Animal Rescue in Brooklyn, New York. See her adoption profile at amaanimalrescue.org and follow the rescue on Instagram @amaanimalrescue and Facebook.

item.title: Bonded Kittens Forced Outside From Safety at Seven Weeks Old Are Learning to Trust, Side by Side
item.description:
Two bonded kitten siblings were put out on the street as tiny babies, far too small to face the world on their own. Now, curled up together in a foster home, they are warm, well-fed, and rarely more than a paw's reach apart.

Billie, all curiosityCredit: Friends of Normie

Mittens and Billie started life in Compton, California, in the care of a kind young man who gave them a roof over their heads. For those first several weeks, the little ones had someone looking out for them and wanted for nothing.

That security did not last. When the kittens were about seven weeks old, the situation in the home changed, and the young man was made to put them outside. It was a hard turn for everyone involved, him included. Far too small to fend for themselves, the frightened babies were spotted and rescued, then placed in the care of Friends of Normie, who put them in a loving foster home.

The two are inseparable, bound by the kind of closeness only siblings share. Mittens is a handsome gray-and-black tabby boy, and his sister Billie is a striking girl with a swirled coat of gray, black, and orange. Wherever one of them wanders, the other is rarely more than a step behind.

Settling inCredit: Friends of Normie

For the first time, Mittens and Billie had everything a kitten should have from the start. There was warmth and safety, full bellies and soft beds, and the steady kindness of people they could trust. Little by little, the pair who had known the uncertainty of the street began to understand that this time, the comfort was there to stay.

As the days passed, their worry gave way to curiosity. They started venturing out to investigate their new surroundings, discovering toys worth chasing and high perches worth climbing, growing bolder and steadier with each day.

Did you see that? Credit: Friends of Normie

Once they felt secure, their personalities began to surface, and the two could not be more different. Mittens is the watchful one, taking his time with new people and new places, and hanging back until he has decided the coast is clear.

What comes after the wait is always worth it. "Mittens is initially the more cautious of the two. But once he feels safe, he blossoms into a sweet, affectionate cuddle bug with a playful, chatty personality," Friends of Normie shared with LoveMeow.

Making himself at homeCredit: Friends of Normie

Billie needs no such warming up. She meets the world head-on, the first to bound toward anything new and to welcome her favorite people the moment they come through the door.

"Billie is curious, affectionate, and full of joyful energy. She loves greeting people with happy little meows and quickly melts into cuddles once she trusts you," Friends of Normie shared. Different as they are, one thing stays constant: their devotion to one another.

Daily exercise routine Credit: Friends of Normie

Mittens and Billie face every new experience side by side, drawing confidence from each other the way only littermates can. They curl up nose to nose to sleep and press close together whenever something unfamiliar comes their way, each one a little braver for having the other near.

Having weathered such an uncertain start together, the two now spend their days doing what safe, happy kittens do, chasing toys across the floor, scaling the cat tree, and stretching out to nap wherever the mood takes them. It all traces back to the second rescue that reached them in time and the foster home that took them in.

Room to grow Credit: Friends of Normie

The home Mittens and Billie were born into couldn't keep them, but through every hard turn, the two had each other, and they still do. Braver by the day, they take on each new thing as a team of two, one leading and one following close behind, neither of them ever alone.

Mittens and Billie Credit: Friends of Normie

Share this story with your friends. Mittens and Billie are being fostered through Friends of Normie. Follow their journey on Instagram @friendsofnormie and Facebook.

item.title: LoveMeow's Best Senior Cat Stories
item.description:
Senior cats are among the most overlooked animals in rescues. They wait longer, get passed over more often, and arrive carrying the weight of years that younger cats have not yet lived. LoveMeow has been reporting original cat rescue and adoption stories since 2014. These are the ten senior cat stories that have resonated most with our readers, sourced directly from shelters, rescue organizations, and foster families across the world.

The 10 Best Senior Cat Stories on LoveMeow

Bilbo Baggins and Super Ted Credit: The Stray Cat Club

1. Two Twelve-Year-Old Cat Brothers Named Bilbo Baggins and Super Ted Were Forced to Start Over and a Caring Foster Helped Their Personalities Shine

Bilbo Baggins and Super Ted had shared every single day of their twelve years together, every nap, every meal, every slow afternoon, side by side. When the only home they had ever known was suddenly gone, the two brothers arrived at The Stray Cat Club carrying something that looked like grief. They were quiet, careful, and still figuring out whether the world they had landed in was safe. Their foster understood that what was happening was not just adjustment. It was loss. She gave them time and consistency, and gradually both cats began to find their footing. Bilbo started exploring. Super Ted began to show the people around him who he had always been.

Read Bilbo and Super Ted's full story

RosieThe Stray Cat Club

2. A Senior Cat Spent Six Years Forgotten in a Basement and the People Who Found Her Made Sure She Knew She Mattered

Rosie had been in the basement of a facility for six years, passed over while younger cats came and went around her. When Ten Lives Club took her in, they placed her in one of the rescue's offices to free roam. The staff called her name, told her she was gorgeous, and meant it every time. She started by watching from beneath the marketing team's desk. Then she began stepping out. She discovered that hands reaching toward her meant something good was coming, that her bowl would always be filled, and that the people in that room were not going anywhere. She has since found a home with a person described as having a heart of gold and endless patience.

Read Rosie's full story

SenecaCredit: AMA Animal Rescue

3. A Senior Cat Arrived at Rescue with One Hour to Spare and Has Spent Two Years Making Sure Nobody Forgets She Is Worth the Wait

Seneca came to AMA Animal Rescue in Brooklyn with one hour left. Every other rescue had said no. AMA said yes. She spent her early days in an oxygen tank fighting back from a severe asthma attack. She won. What emerged once she was stable, was a cat with a personality that stops everyone who meets her. She meows to remind people that hand pets are overdue, poses for photos with obvious intention, and chases her toy fish with the concentration of a cat who has serious business to attend to. Two years later, she is still waiting for the right person, and she has not stopped announcing her availability for a single day.

Read Seneca's full story

Cosmic Cowboy and Bo PeepCredit: TailsHigh

4. A Ten-Year-Old Cat Named Cosmic Cowboy Arrived Severely Neglected and Helped a Shy Cat Named Bo Peep Learn to Trust

Cosmic Cowboy arrived at Tails High after years of severe neglect, covered in fleas, matted from head to tail, and so weighed down by accumulated fur and debris that his balance was affected. He fell over when he tried to walk or make biscuits. The veterinary team stayed late to care for him. Over months, his coat grew back, and his confidence returned. Then a shy cat named Bo Peep arrived at Tails High with her kittens. She was a devoted mother but remained extremely wary of people, hiding from human contact long after her kittens had grown and moved on. The staff introduced her to Cosmic Cowboy, a cat who adored human companionship. His steady, confident presence gave Bo Peep the reassurance she needed. The two hit it off immediately, and Bo Peep began to come forward in ways she never had before.

Read Cosmic Cowboy and Bo Peep's full story

SteveCredit: Thrifted Kittens Animal Rescue

5. A Worker Found a Cat Named Steve Living Among Strays with Few Teeth, a Bent Ear, and a Heart of Gold

Steve was found living among a colony of strays, looking rough around the edges, with few teeth, a bent ear, and the kind of face that comes from years of outdoor living. A worker spotted him and contacted Thrifted Kittens Animal Rescue. Steve came in without complaint, received the care he needed, and settled into foster life with the ease of a cat who had been waiting for exactly this. He turned out to be a champion cuddler, devoted to laps and deeply appreciative of anyone who sat still long enough for him to climb onto them. He found his home not long after.

Read Steve's full story

GarCredit: TNR North Platte

6. A Senior Cat Named Gar Spent Years at a Trailer Park in North Platte, Nebraska with Almost No Teeth and Not a Single Complaint

Gar had been a fixture at a trailer park in North Platte, Nebraska for years, one of those cats everyone knew and few people truly looked after. A kind woman and her daughter had been feeding him, but when they had to move, Gar was suddenly without anyone. Sami Smith and her team at TNR North Platte arrived at the trailer park to do trap-neuter-return work, and Gar walked right up to them, as friendly as could be. He had lost most of his teeth to infection over the years but had clearly decided that was not worth dwelling on. He went into foster care and moved through his new environment with the unhurried confidence of a cat who had spent eleven years figuring out exactly who he was.

Read Gar's full story

LilithCredit: Angela Smith Schwartz

7. A Senior Cat Named Lilith Who Greeted Her Rescuer with a Hiss Turned Out to Have the Most to Say Once Someone Finally Listened

Lilith was found outside in South Florida covered in flea bites, her skin raw from a flea allergy that had been tormenting her for an unknown length of time. She was not a cat who had been outdoors for a few weeks. She was a cat who had been managing. When Angela, a foster with Good Karma Pet Rescue, walked over to say hello, Lilith hissed. Angela left a humane trap, and Lilith has been with her ever since. Once indoors and free of fleas, something unlocked. Lilith moved through the space like a cat who remembered exactly what a home was, because she had clearly lived in one before she was abandoned. She takes a daily thyroid medication that disappears into her food the moment it arrives, because mealtimes are the undisputed highlight of her day and she is not subtle about it. When she is relaxed, she flings a toy across the room and chases it like a kitten. She has not stopped talking since the day someone finally gave her the chance.

Read Lilith's full story

JulieCredit: FieldHaven Feline Center

8. A 21-Year-Old Cat Lost the Only Home She Had Ever Known and Wonderful People Promised Her the Best Rest of Her Life

Julie had lived with the same family since she was young. When her elderly owner passed away, Julie found herself outside the house she had shared with one person for twenty-one years, with no understanding of what had happened. Noah, who had known Julie for all those years, sent an urgent rescue request that reached Lisa of the FieldHaven Animal Support Team. That night, Joy Smith posted a plea for a foster. By morning, Amelia had responded. She wrote two words: "I will." The next day, Lisa braved severe weather to transport Julie to the rescue. Julie arrived and never looked back.

Read Julie's full story

SammyCredit: Purrfect Pals Cat Sanctuary and Adoption Centers

9. An 18-Year-Old Cat Asked a Man to Take Him Home and the Two Have Been Together Ever Since

Sammy was 18 years old when Purrfect Pals Cat Sanctuary and Adoption Centers in Arlington, Washington, rescued him from a public shelter after his owner could no longer keep him. The rescue described him as a mellow gentleman in a spiffy tuxedo coat, adept at handling whatever life brought his way. Tim Adams, who had a senior cat of his own, came to see Sammy at the adoption center. He found him sitting alone, looking a little dejected. When Tim walked up, Sammy rubbed his face against Tim's hands over and over. Tim adopted him that day. Two years later, Sammy turned 20.

Read Sammy and Tim's full story

BennyCredit: LoogaBeluga

10. An 11-Year-Old Cat Had Been in the Shelter for Ten Years and When He Finally Found His Person He Held Her Hands Through the Cage Bars

Benny was 11 years old when his person found him, which means he had been at the shelter since he was approximately one year old. Somehow, a decade had passed, and nobody had taken him home. When a woman came to the shelter searching for a cat, she had visited several times before without finding her match. Then she reached Benny's kennel. He perked up, reached through the bars, and held her hands with his paws. She looked at the volunteer and said she would take him. The volunteer was surprised by how fast it happened. Benny was not. He had been waiting ten years for exactly that moment, and he was not about to let it pass without making his intentions absolutely clear.

Read Benny's full story

What Makes a Senior Cat Story Unforgettable?

The senior cat stories that move readers most share a common thread. Someone chose to show up for a cat that most people had walked past. They made room, learned what that cat needed, and gave them the time to find their footing. The cats, in return, gave everything they had.

LoveMeow reports original senior cat stories regularly, sourced directly from rescuers, foster families, shelters, and the people who open their homes to cats that others overlooked. Browse all senior cat coverage in our Rescue section and News section.

Senior cats are statistically adopted at significantly lower rates than younger cats and kittens. item.title: Calico Mama Cat and Her Two Roly Poly Babies Are Growing Big and Strong in the Care of a Devoted Foster
item.description:
Two newborn kittens became so round from all their milk that they roll right out of bed. Their Mama isn't worried because she's trained her carers well.

Cassava, Sago, and TapiocaCredit: Best Friends Felines

Cassava and her babies came into the care of Best Friends Felines, a volunteer-run cat rescue in south-east Queensland, Australia, after one of the rescue's veterinary-nurse carers reached out for help. A colleague at her clinic had taken in a mama cat and her litter, and the rescue moved quickly, placing the family with Jen, one of its carers who specializes in mothers and their newborn kittens.

The family had already known sorrow. When the carers collected them, they learned that one of the tiny babies had not made it, lost to a severe cleft palate. The brave mama and her two remaining kittens were bundled gently into a carrier and driven to the warm foster room waiting for them.

From the moment they arrived, the little family began to flourish. Cassava is a stunning fluffy calico with a heart full of devotion, and she settled in fast, doting on her two precious little beans with endless patience.

Never far from her side Credit: Best Friends Felines

One of her babies is a tiny mirror image of her, a sweet tortoiseshell, and the other is an adorable ginger-and-white kitten who completes the little trio.

Because the two were still too small to tell whether the ginger-and-white one was a boy or a girl, the carers chose a food theme and matching unisex names. The family became Cassava, Tapioca, and Sago.

Tapioca and Sago Credit: Best Friends Felines

With only two babies now sharing the milk bar, Tapioca and Sago have been growing deliciously chunky. By just two weeks old, both were already tipping the scales at close to three hundred and fifty grams.

Sago at three and a half weeks Credit: Best Friends Felines

All that healthy eating has left them wonderfully roly-poly, so round that, once or twice, a well-fed little one has rolled straight out of bed. "Of course, mumma closes her eyes and pretends it hasn't happened and awaits her well-trained people to pick them up and put them back into bed," Jen, the family's foster carer, shared with LoveMeow.

Belly full and dreaming Credit: Best Friends Felines

As the babies have grown more independent, Cassava has begun taking a few well-earned moments to herself. Every so often she pads out of the nursery to find Jen, weaving around her for a top-up of food or a chin scratch, and sometimes just for a quiet minute away from her busy babies. She has especially loved soaking up pats while Jen works from home, and she has taken every new visitor completely in her stride.

The weeks since have brought delightful changes. "It is hard to believe that the babies are already 3.5 weeks old, but then you watch their cheeky little faces as they stand up and toddle around," Jen shared. The pair are still gaining beautifully, inching close to five hundred grams and getting rounder by the day.

Tapioca, growing fast Credit: Best Friends Felines

Cassava is comfortable spending longer stretches away now, happily napping or topping up on food to keep pace with her busy babies.

Tapioca and Sago, meanwhile, are becoming little explorers, sitting up to survey the room, hopping in and out of their bed, and starting to play with each other.

Cassava, the wonderful MomCredit: Best Friends Felines

Ever the protective mother, Cassava is still a little wary of the other cats she can glimpse through the special gates on her door, so introductions will wait until she is ready. "We know that mums are very protective of their babies, so it will be a while before proper introductions," Jen shared.

A quiet moment togetherCredit: Best Friends Felines

Not long ago, Cassava arrived at her foster room with two tiny babies and an uncertain road ahead. Now she is a picture of calm, doting on two round, happy kittens and trusting her people to handle the occasional roll out of bed.

Share this story with your friends. View more on Cassava, Tapioca, and Sago, who are in the care of Best Friends Felines. Follow their progress on Instagram @bestfriendsfelines and on Facebook.

item.title: Kitten Was Only Supposed to Be Trapped and Released, but Chose Purring and Biscuits Over Going Back Outside
item.description:
An outdoor kitten was only supposed to be trapped and released. Instead, she chose to begin purring and making biscuits in the cage and decided she wasn't going back outside.

MistyCredit: For Animals Inc.

Misty's story began in Jamaica, Queens, at the end of June, where she was trapped as part of a trap, neuter, and return project. Even in that trap, this gentle girl showed exactly who she was, purring away and happily making biscuits with her little paws, sweet as could be despite her uncertain situation.

Her rescue speaks to a hard reality that cat rescuers across New York City face every day. With shelters and foster homes stretched far beyond capacity, dedicated trappers are sometimes forced to make the painful choice to spay and release even the friendliest cats, because there is nowhere left for them to go. "We are so over capacity that at this point we have to make the difficult decision to TNR friendly cats and kittens," For Animals Inc., a volunteer-run cat rescue in Queens, shared with LoveMeow.

Misty had been on that very path, one of the hardest parts of the work these rescuers do. But this little one was about to get lucky, all because of one person's compassion.

Purring in the trapCredit: For Animals Inc.

Another volunteer caught sight of Misty in the trap, purring and kneading, and could not bear to let her go. Even though she already had far too many cats in her care, she opened her home to give Misty a chance at the life she deserved.

Instead of heading back out to the streets, Misty was headed into foster care with a brighter future ahead.

A face full of sweetnessCredit: For Animals Inc.

Safe at last, Misty blossomed into a wonderful little companion, and it is easy to see why everyone who meets her falls for her. She is affectionate to her core, purring the moment a person so much as glances her way, as if she cannot contain how glad she is to be seen.

She is spirited and playful, too. Misty loves her ball tower and her wand toys, and she adores playing with other cats.

Waiting on her next mealCredit: For Animals Inc.

One of the sweetest parts of her foster life is her bond with her foster brother Pepita, another friendly cat rescued from Jamaica, Queens earlier this year. The two have become the best of friends, grooming each other and curling up to sleep together.

Almost got it! Credit: For Animals Inc.

Now around five months old, Misty is spayed, fully vaccinated, and healthy, and she has tested negative for FIV and FeLV. She is wonderful with other cats and dogs, and by every account, completely ready for a home of her own.

Misty has now been waiting for a home longer than anyone expected. "We cannot believe Misty is still waiting for her forever home," the rescue shared.

She has turned out to be one of the most uncomplicated cats the rescue has fostered. A warm bed, a full bowl, a lap to purr on, and the company of another cat or two, and she is perfectly content.

Not long ago, Misty was purring in a trap, moments from being spayed and sent back out to the streets she came from. Today she is safe, healthy, and thoroughly herself, waiting in a foster home for the one person ready to see what everyone around her already has.

item.title: Five Colony Kittens Needed Gloves To Handle for Only Two Days Before Deciding They Preferred Purring on Laps
item.description:
A litter of five feral kittens could not be picked up without a pair of thick gloves. Now they seek out human hands on their own, leaning into scratches and purring on laps.

AcornCredit: Sonora Cat Rescue

Their story unfolds at a home where Sadie Anderson, president of Sonora Cat Rescue, an all-volunteer cat rescue in Sonora, California, has been trapping for two full years. The cats there have always been especially feral and hard to catch, and the elderly homeowners, who lovingly feed the colony, are unable to do the trapping themselves. Over the years, the same mama cat has had at least three litters on the property, and the rescue has worked steadily to help each one.

When the new babies turned up, the homeowners knew exactly who to call. Sadie headed over to size up the new litter, but as anyone who has worked with feral cats knows, this kind of work takes patience. On the first night, only a single kitten could be trapped. She was gently brought home to begin her new life in foster care.

Sadie returned the next night with more equipment and more time, and it paid off. Two more kittens and their mama were trapped; the babies joined their sibling in foster care, and the mother was spayed and released the next day with an ear tip to mark her as cared for. Two kitten traps were left out overnight and then caught the final two, and the entire litter was safely in.

How they started out Credit: Sonora Cat Rescue

The work did not stop there. Returning to help the last of the colony, Sadie trapped two older teenage kittens from an earlier litter, who were ear-tipped and released. Only the elusive papa cat still slips past the traps, but with the same determination that carried the rest of the effort, Sadie is confident he will turn up eventually, and this colony can finally be closed for good.

For the new rescued and appointed 'Squash' babies, the most remarkable part was beginning. Sadie named the litter after squash, with Acorn and Spaghetti the first two to earn their names, and calls the whole crew her spice nuggets. What she understands about young kittens matters here: there is a narrow window, early in life, when a feral kitten can still learn to trust, and it does not stay open long.

Spaghetti and ButterNutCredit: Sonora Cat Rescue

"When kittens are 5 to 8 weeks old, their personalities are very malleable. In rescue, we rush to capitalize on that formative window and socialize them hard," Sadie shared with LoveMeow.

"Once they get to be around 9 weeks old, that window slams shut." After that, taming a feral kitten can take far longer, and some stay fearful for the rest of their lives.

Socialization in effect Credit: Sonora Cat Rescue

That is exactly why these kittens were given focused, one-on-one attention the moment they arrived. At only six weeks old, each spent its first days apart from the others, getting food and play only in Sadie's company, so that a person became the source of every good thing in their day.

SpaghettiCredit: Sonora Cat Rescue

The change came astonishingly fast. "It hasn't even been 2 full days, and these spice nuggets I couldn't grab without gloves are now approaching me, leaning into scritches, and even purring," Sadie shared. Kittens who days earlier had shrunk into a crack in the concrete were now climbing into a lap for attention.

It is a vivid reminder of how quickly patience and the right timing can rewrite a frightened kitten's whole idea of people. A week on, the once-wild litter is fully at ease, tumbling and play-fighting like any other kittens.

Reunited and it feels good Credit: Sonora Cat Rescue

Soon the Squash babies will be confident enough to stay together as a group, even when Sadie is away, without slipping back into their feral ways. And once their quarantine is finished, a bigger reunion awaits. "Once quarantine is done, they can combine with the Cheers gang and be a giant happy family," Sadie shared, folding the litter into another group of rescued cats to make one large, contented crew.

None of it would have been possible without the elderly homeowners, whose years of faithfully feeding the colony kept these cats alive long enough to be reached. With people no longer something to fear, the little ones have thrown themselves into being kittens, wrestling and chasing and pouncing across their foster room.

PattyPanCredit: Sonora Cat Rescue

The scared faces from the colony are gone, replaced by a litter of playful, purring cats who have decided the world is a friendly place after all. For the Squash babies, the hardest part is already behind them.

Not long ago, the Squash babies were a knot of feral kittens wedged into a gap in a wall, too wild to touch. Now they are purring, playing, and climbing into laps, a litter of little squash growing braver by the day.

Acorn and ZucchiniCredit: Sonora Cat Rescue

Share this story with your friends. View more on the Squash babies and Sonora Cat Rescue, an all-volunteer cat rescue serving Sonora and Tuolumne County, California. Follow their rescue and socialization work on Instagram @sonoracatrescue and on Facebook. Special thanks to Sadie Anderson @wfhfoster.

item.title: Kitten Found Abandoned in a Cardboard Box Now Spends Her Days Bossing Around a Dog Many Times Her Size
item.description:
A tiny kitten was found alone in a cardboard box, left out on a public green with no mother or siblings in sight. Now she spends her days bossing around a gentle giant of a dog, who outweighs her many times over.

Dove TreeCredit: The Stray Cat Club

Dove's story began in the saddest of circumstances. This little girl was discovered completely alone, tucked inside a cardboard box and left behind on a public green. There was no mother and no siblings anywhere to be found, and however she came to be there, this tiny kitten had been abandoned, left to face the world entirely on her own.

Kindness found her just in time. A passerby came across the little one, could not bear to leave her alone, and carried her to someone they knew who had cats and could keep her safe for the moment. That person put out an appeal for help, and when The Stray Cat Club, a cat rescue charity in South East London, saw it, the rescue stepped in without hesitation.

When Dove arrived in the rescue's care, her condition made clear just how much she needed them. She weighed only two hundred and eighty-eight grams, so impossibly small that at first everyone assumed she was two or three weeks old. It soon became clear that she was actually closer to five weeks, and seriously malnourished.

Safe and warmCredit: The Stray Cat Club

It was a sobering realization. At an age when she should have been growing, playing, and learning alongside her mother and littermates, this brave little girl had instead been quietly surviving at a fraction of the size she was meant to be.

All of that is behind her now, because Dove landed exactly where she needed to be. Surrounded by people determined to help her thrive, she has been given regular meals, warmth, and round-the-clock care, including the gentle, hands-on tending a fragile kitten requires.

A much-needed bathCredit: The Stray Cat Club

Dove is loving her meals, tucking into each one with the enthusiasm of a kitten who is finally getting everything she needs. Most of all, she is steadily gaining weight. "Dove is safe, absolutely loving having regular meals and, most importantly, steadily gaining weight," The Stray Cat Club shared with LoveMeow.

For the people watching over her, every gram gained is a small victory. And as she starts to feel better, something delightful has begun to happen: her funny little personality is shining through more and more, a sure sign of a kitten who feels safe enough to be herself.

Never missing a meal nowCredit: The Stray Cat Club

This pint-sized charmer, it turns out, has plenty of spunk to spare. One of her new favorite pastimes is bossing around the resident dog, a gentle giant many, many times her size. "We're also beginning to see her funny little personality shining through more and more each day, including bullying the resident 40kg dog," the rescue shared.

Watching a tiny scrap of a kitten fearlessly order around a forty-kilogram dog, nearly a hundred and forty times her weight, is enough to make anyone laugh. It is also a joyful reminder of how far she has already come.

Bossing her gentle giantCredit: The Stray Cat Club

Dove still has plenty of growing and catching up to do, and no one pretends otherwise. But she is not doing it alone, not anymore. The people caring for her put it plainly, in words addressed straight to her. "You've got plenty of growing and catching up to do, little one, but you've got us behind you every step of the way," the rescue shared.

Behind her is an entire team of devoted rescuers giving her all the time and patience she needs. Little by little, it is working, and the scrap of a kitten from the cardboard box is turning into a bright, feisty little girl, a bit stronger and a bit bolder with each passing day.

Finally able to restCredit: The Stray Cat Club

Not long ago, Dove Tree was a two-hundred-and-eighty-eight-gram kitten alone in a cardboard box, surviving at a fraction of the size she should have been. Now she is warm, well fed, and gaining by the day, with a whole team in her corner and a giant dog to boss around.

Warm and cozyCredit: The Stray Cat Club

item.title: Snaggle-Toothed Cat Lost His Home of Five Years, but His Nose for Treats Led Him Straight to a New One
item.description:
Reese is an orange cat with a snaggle tooth, a face that looks permanently offended, and a deep conviction that every bag, purse, and pocket in the room is hiding a treat with his name on it. After landing back at his rescue for a second time, he has finally won over someone who saw all of that and chose him anyway.

ReeseCredit: Orphans of the Storm

Reese's history with the rescue goes back a few years. He first came to Orphans of the Storm in 2021 as a stray kitten from Mundelein, Illinois, and it was not long before he was adopted into a home of his own. He spent nearly five happy years there until, at the end of August and through no fault of his own, he was returned when his family's circumstances changed.

Coming back after so long could have been a sad chapter. Instead, the team at Orphans of the Storm, a no-kill shelter in Chicago's northern suburbs that has been finding homes for animals since 1928, was overjoyed to have this remarkable boy in their care again. They knew exactly how special he was, and they set out to find him a loving home for the second time.

And what a personality Reese has. "He is seriously one of the most fun, quirky, and sweet cats," Orphans of the Storm shared with LoveMeow. He is wonderfully curious and just a little nosy, certain that every bag in the room might be hiding a snack meant for him.

Reese as a kittenCredit: Orphans of the Storm

His investigative habits became the stuff of legend around the shelter. A purse was something to climb into. A bag had to be checked. A coat pocket was deeply suspicious and worth a thorough search.

And the moment something crinkled, that was as good as a search warrant for this determined little detective. When he was not busy going through someone's belongings, he was happy to play, eat well, and stretch out to enjoy the good life.

Keeping WatchCredit: Orphans of the Storm

Then there is the famous tooth. Reese's snaggle tooth is exactly the way it is meant to be, a perfectly healthy little quirk, and it makes his already expressive face impossible to look at without laughing.

The tooth is only half of it. Paired with an expression of lofty, dignified disapproval, it gives Reese a look entirely his own. "Despite looking like a tiny man who has been inconvenienced for the last time, Reese is actually the sweetest, most affectionate guy," the rescue shared.

Deeply unimpressedCredit: Orphans of the Storm

Anyone who spent even a minute with him knew the truth. He loved attention, adored his people, and made wonderful company, and he just happened to wear a face that suggested otherwise.

The shelter shared his story far and wide, celebrating his nosy antics and his one-of-a-kind face, and hoping the right person would look past the grumpy little mug and see the treasure underneath.

Make sure you get my good side Credit: Orphans of the Storm

And then, while his story was still making the rounds, the best possible thing happened. Reese, the little snaggle-toothed menace who looked perpetually offended and needed to know what was inside every purse, bag, and pocket, was officially adopted.

In the end, a family looked at that gloriously grumpy face, that endless curiosity, and that heart of pure gold, and decided he was exactly the cat they wanted, snaggle tooth, offended expression, nosiness and all. "Somebody actually saw all of that and said, 'Yep. I want that one,'" the rescue shared.

Adopted and heading homeCredit: Orphans of the Storm

After everything, the cat whose expressions suggested he was always moments from filing a complaint had won someone over completely, exactly as he was. The team that welcomed him back, cared for him, and loved him through his second search had finally seen him off to the home he so richly deserved.

Reese now has a family of his own, a whole new house to inspect, and an entirely new set of people to inconvenience.

Home for goodCredit: Orphans of the Storm

Reese spent a long time being exactly himself, a little nosy, a little offended-looking, and impossibly sweet, waiting for the person who would see all of him. Now he is home for good, chosen for every quirk, and almost certainly already investigating every bag in the house.

Share this story with your friends. View more on Reese and learn more about Orphans of the Storm on Facebook or on Instagram @orphansofthestorm.

And what a personality Reese has. "He is seriously one of the most fun, quirky, and sweet cats," Orphans of the Storm shared with LoveMeow. He is wonderfully curious and just a little nosy, certain that every bag in the room might be hiding a snack meant for him.

Reese as a kittenCredit: Orphans of the Storm

His investigative habits became the stuff of legend around the shelter. A purse was something to climb into. A bag had to be checked. A coat pocket was deeply suspicious and worth a thorough search.

And the moment something crinkled, that was as good as a search warrant for this determined little detective. When he was not busy going through someone's belongings, he was happy to play, eat well, and stretch out to enjoy the good life.

Keeping WatchCredit: Orphans of the Storm

Then there is the famous tooth. Reese's snaggle tooth is exactly the way it is meant to be, a perfectly healthy little quirk, and it makes his already expressive face impossible to look at without laughing.

The tooth is only half of it. Paired with an expression of lofty, dignified disapproval, it gives Reese a look entirely his own. "Despite looking like a tiny man who has been inconvenienced for the last time, Reese is actually the sweetest, most affectionate guy," the rescue shared.

Deeply unimpressedCredit: Orphans of the Storm

Anyone who spent even a minute with him knew the truth. He loved attention, adored his people, and made wonderful company, and he just happened to wear a face that suggested otherwise.

The shelter shared his story far and wide, celebrating his nosy antics and his one-of-a-kind face, and hoping the right person would look past the grumpy little mug and see the treasure underneath.

Make sure you get my good side Credit: Orphans of the Storm

And then, while his story was still making the rounds, the best possible thing happened. Reese, the little snaggle-toothed menace who looked perpetually offended and needed to know what was inside every purse, bag, and pocket, was officially adopted.

In the end, a family looked at that gloriously grumpy face, that endless curiosity, and that heart of pure gold, and decided he was exactly the cat they wanted, snaggle tooth, offended expression, nosiness and all. "Somebody actually saw all of that and said, 'Yep. I want that one,'" the rescue shared.

Adopted and heading homeCredit: Orphans of the Storm

After everything, the cat whose expressions suggested he was always moments from filing a complaint had won someone over completely, exactly as he was. The team that welcomed him back, cared for him, and loved him through his second search had finally seen him off to the home he so richly deserved.

Reese now has a family of his own, a whole new house to inspect, and an entirely new set of people to inconvenience.

Home for goodCredit: Orphans of the Storm

Reese spent a long time being exactly himself, a little nosy, a little offended-looking, and impossibly sweet, waiting for the person who would see all of him. Now he is home for good, chosen for every quirk, and almost certainly already investigating every bag in the house.

item.description:

DominicCredit: Bengal Rescue

Frightened, he squeezed himself beneath the bridge into a cramped and dangerous space with cars thundering past overhead. His rescuer, Karen, reached him, pulled him free, and brought him into foster care. The foster family who took him in paid close attention to what he needed: a four-legged companion who could match his energy. He found one in a resident dog, and the two have been inseparable since. Ponti is neutered, fully vetted, and looking for a family with a furry friend already waiting.

Read Ponti's full story

MeowthCredit: Meow Parlour

4. A Three-Legged Cat Spent 16 Months at New York City's First Cat Cafe and Finally Made It to His Forever Home

Meowth spent 16 months at Meow Parlour, New York City's first cat cafe, charming every visitor who walked through the door without ever quite convincing one to take him home. Three legs did nothing to slow him down. His fosters described him as active and friendly, almost like a dog: a cat who followed you from room to room, narrated his opinions, and turned every tunnel and tent into his personal headquarters. His adoption was ultimately sponsored by Cat Video Fest and Oscilloscope Labs as part of their partnership with Meow Parlour to help the cafe's hardest-to-place cats find homes. After 16 months, Meowth has his.

Read Meowth's full story

RockyCredit: SCRATCH, Inc.

5. A Kitten Was Found Buried Under a Pile of Rocks Inside a Drain Pipe, and the Moment He Was Pulled Free He Started to Purr

Rocky was found inside a drain pipe near the Hixson YMCA in Chattanooga, Tennessee, buried under a pile of heavy rocks, crying in the dark. Holly, a volunteer with SCRATCH, Inc., and her husband headed out late on a Friday night to trace the sound to its source. They found him, moved the rocks, and lifted him out. She came in with three kittens alongside her, and settled into foster care on her own terms and her own timeline. The foster family gave her exactly that. Black cats are statistically among the least likely to be adopted, two-thirds less likely than white cats and half as likely as tabbies. Simon's story began with someone saying yes to the overlooked one. Nine years in, it is still going.

item.title: Seven Orange Tabby Kittens Found Under a Fallen Tree at a Senior Home Are a Happy Challenge to Tell Apart
item.description:
A mama cat and her seven tiny kittens were found living under a fallen tree at a senior living facility in Indianapolis, and a rescue team reached them within fifteen minutes of the call. Now safe and warm in foster care, the whole family has been christened the Golden Years Gang, each one named after a grandparent.

Millie and her babiesCredit: Lori White

Their rescue began with a call for help. Word came in about a mother cat and her seven little ones who had been getting by beneath a fallen tree at a senior living facility on the south side of Indianapolis. It was no place for a family of eight.

When a rescuer with Alliance for Responsible Pet Ownership, a foster-based rescue in Indianapolis, arrived and surveyed the scene, there was no saying no. She got straight on the phone.

The response was immediate. "We couldn't say no to helping them, so we quickly made some calls, and within 15 minutes my husband and daughter arrived with old towels, Churus, and carriers," Lori White, the ARPO foster now caring for the family, shared with LoveMeow.

The rescue Credit: Lori White

With old towels for warmth, Churu treats to coax the cats out, and carriers ready to go, the little team gathered up the whole family in one swift, careful effort.

Momma and all seven babies were carried away from the outdoors for good. It was the kind of day that leaves a rescuer grateful for the friends and family who show up without hesitation when a family of cats needs them most.

LoveMeow may earn a small commission from purchases made through links in this article at no additional cost to you.

Tucked into the hollowCredit: Lori White

Once they were safe, the little family inspired a naming theme as charming as the rescue itself. Lori thought it over through the rest of the evening, and by the time she had washed the rescue dirt out of her hair, she had landed on a Golden Years Gang theme, a nod to the senior living facility where the family had been found. Each cat got a wonderfully old-fashioned name to match.

At the head of the family is Momma Mildred, Millie for short. Her seven kittens are five boys, Norman, Stanley, Bernard, Eugene, and Otis Henry, and two little girls, Dottie and Pearl Louise.

The whole boy gangCredit: Lori White

The kittens are only about two and a half to three weeks old, tiny and precious, and just beginning to explore the world from the safety of their foster home.

Telling all those little faces apart has become a happy challenge. "Five ginger boys with matching baby faces did not get the memo about making my job easier," Lori shared with us. Even so, a system has emerged: Stanley is the lone blondie, big Bernard is the largest and darkest of the brothers, and little Norman, the smallest, has the long fur that gives him away.

Sound asleep togetherCredit: Lori White

And Momma Millie is flourishing. After going without proper nutrition while living outdoors, she is eating with real gusto. "We have no doubt she is trying to make up for all the nutrients she wasn't getting while living outdoors," Lori shared.

She is pouring all of it back into her babies, and it shows in every content, well-fed kitten curled up against her. She is being a Mom, by every measure, in every part of the word.

Sweet dreams Credit: Lori White

Now that they are indoors, the whole family is enjoying the small comforts they went so long without. They are safe, they are warm, their bellies are full, and they are wrapped in the attention they missed for so long.

For a mama who worked so hard to keep her babies alive against the elements, it is an enormous relief. She can finally rest, knowing her family is in good hands.

One big cuddle puddle Credit: Lori White

Not long ago, Millie was raising seven kittens alone beneath a fallen tree, doing everything she could to keep them warm and fed. Now the whole Golden Years Gang is indoors, full-bellied and safe, with nothing left to do but grow up surrounded by love.

For a family that started with nothing but each other, it is the softest of landings, and the best of their story is still ahead.

Mama MillieCredit: Lori White

Share this story with your friends. View more on Millie and her Golden Years Gang journey with Lori White on Instagram @dreaming_of_foster_kittens, and learn more about ARPO at arporescue.org.

item.title: Cat Passed From Home to Home Was Reunited With His Rescue by a Microchip, and Now Holds Hands When Pet
item.description:
A gray cat who moved from home to home for years is reunited with his original rescue thanks to a kind woman and his microchip. Now he holds hands with whoever gives him sweet pets.

Truly ScrumptiousCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

Truly Scrumptious, or Truly for short, is a sweet four-year-old gray cat whose story began happily enough. He was adopted as a kitten in 2022 from Whiskers-A-GoGo, an all-volunteer cat rescue in Brooklyn, and sent off with every hope for a wonderful life.

The years that followed took some hard turns. About a year after the adoption, the woman who took him home split with her boyfriend, and he kept the cat, even though she had signed the adoption papers. A few years later, he moved to an apartment that did not allow pets and left Truly with his elderly mother.

Before long, that woman's landlord stopped by to say that pets were not permitted there. With nowhere left to turn, she tucked Truly into a granny cart, piled her shopping bags on top of him, and set out to leave him on the street.

Able to rest at lastCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

On her way, she thankfully passed Good Home Cat Adoptions, a small rescue storefront on Franklin Avenue in Crown Heights, run by a rescuer named Bronwen. Bronwen took the cat in, and rather than sending him on to the city shelter, she did one small but important thing: she scanned him for a microchip.

That single decision changed everything. When Bronwen called the microchip company, the scan came back registered to a rescue, and not just any rescue, but Whiskers-A-GoGo, the very group that had sent Truly home as a kitten a few years earlier. Instead of heading to the city shelter, he was going back to the people who had cared about him all along.

Back where he belongsCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

Bronwen kept Truly safe until Whiskers-A-GoGo could come and pick him up. The rescue had never stopped counting him as one of their own, and they had him checked over from nose to tail before settling him into a foster home.

The cat who came back to them was not the confident boy they remembered. For the first few days he was very scared, quiet, and withdrawn, worn thin by being passed along so many times.

Settled in foster careCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

The change took about three weeks. Little by little the fear loosened its grip, the old Truly began to resurface, and the withdrawn cat who had arrived turned back into a happy one.

And what a cat he is. "Truly is gorgeous, cuddly, affectionate, playful, and independent," Whiskers-A-GoGo shared with LoveMeow, describing a boy who offers companionship and easygoing charm in equal measure.

A cuddlebug through and throughCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

He has some especially endearing habits, too. He plays fetch with his mouse toys, trotting each one back and dropping it at his person's feet for another throw, clever and delighted every time. He loves sleeping in bed alongside his people just as much.

The sweetest habit of all comes when he settles in for a cuddle. "He will even reach out to put his paws on your hands and hold them while you cuddle," the rescue shared.

Ready for foreverCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

For a cat who spent so long without a place to call his own, Truly has landed softly in foster care, healthy, affectionate, and content. Whiskers-A-GoGo put its hope for him plainly. "After being passed around for years, this boy deserves a person who means forever when they say it," the rescue shared.

Without that microchip, Truly might have vanished for good, left on a sidewalk or swallowed up by the city shelter system with no way to trace where he came from. It comes down to the tiny chip Whiskers-A-GoGo had registered when he was a kitten, and to Bronwen, who took him in and thought to reach for a scanner.

Truly in his placeCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

Truly Scrumptious spent years being handed from one place to the next, each home slipping away before it could become permanent. Now he is back with the rescue that never stopped being his, and the granny cart and the Brooklyn sidewalk are the last hard chapter of his story.

Share this story with your friends. View more about Truly Scrumptious and Whiskers-A-GoGo on Instagram @whiskers_agogo or on Facebook.

That single decision changed everything. When Bronwen called the microchip company, the scan came back registered to a rescue, and not just any rescue, but Whiskers-A-GoGo, the very group that had sent Truly home as a kitten a few years earlier. Bronwen kept Truly safe until Whiskers-A-GoGo could come and pick him up. The rescue had never stopped counting him as one of their own, and they had him checked over from nose to tail before settling him into a foster home.

The change took about three weeks. Little by little the fear loosened its grip, the old Truly began to resurface, and the withdrawn cat who had arrived turned back into a happy one.

He has some especially endearing habits, too. He plays fetch with his mouse toys, trotting each one back and dropping it at his person's feet for another throw, clever and delighted every time. He loves sleeping in bed alongside his people just as much.

The sweetest habit of all comes when he settles in for a cuddle. "He will even reach out to put his paws on your hands and hold them while you cuddle," the rescue shared.

Ready for foreverCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

For a cat who spent so long without a place to call his own, Truly has landed softly in foster care, healthy, affectionate, and content. Whiskers-A-GoGo put its hope for him plainly. "After being passed around for years, this boy deserves a person who means forever when they say it," the rescue shared.

Without that microchip, Truly might have vanished for good, left on a sidewalk or swallowed up by the city shelter system with no way to trace where he came from. It comes down to the tiny chip Whiskers-A-GoGo had registered when he was a kitten, and to Bronwen, who took him in and thought to reach for a scanner.

Truly in his placeCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

Truly Scrumptious spent years being handed from one place to the next, each home slipping away before it could become permanent. Now he is back with the rescue that never stopped being his, and the granny cart and the Brooklyn sidewalk are the last hard chapter of his story.

item.title: Bonded Kittens From a Packed Shelter Now Spend Their Nights Watching True Crime, Unbothered by a Plot Twist
item.description:
Two bonded kitten siblings were pulled from a crowded shelter and landed somewhere far cozier. Now their favorite way to spend an evening is stretched out along the back of the couch, quietly watching true crime documentaries with their foster.

Mahi Mahi and MackerelCredit: Orphan Kitten Project

Mahi Mahi and Mackerel came into rescue after a local shelter, packed well past its comfortable limit, put out a call for help. With so many animals arriving at once, the shelter hoped to find these two a softer place to land, and reached out to ask whether any foster homes might be open.

That call reached Orphan Kitten Project, a vet student-run rescue at UC Davis, California, that runs entirely on foster homes and has no shelter building of its own. "We are 100% foster-based, so we do not have a shelter facility. When we take in kittens, they are always placed in a foster home," Orphan Kitten Project shared with LoveMeow.

For a group that loves nothing more than getting kittens out of crowded shelters and into real homes, the answer was an easy yes. The two siblings were placed with a devoted foster, and in her care they settled in and began to blossom.

Mellow to the coreCredit: Orphan Kitten Project

Mahi Mahi and Mackerel turned out to be the most wonderfully easygoing pair. They are sweet, mellow, and delightfully low-key, the kind of kittens who bring a calm presence into a room, and they seldom meow, choosing instead to gaze up with big eyes when they would like to be scooped up for a cuddle.

Their foster calls them easy keepers, content to entertain themselves for hours. "They are not destructive or demanding, and can keep themselves entertained as long as they are supplied with a scratcher and each other," the rescue shared. That last part matters most, because their bond sits at the very center of who they are.

Favorite toyCredit: Orphan Kitten Project

Their laid-back charm is only half the story. Hand either of them a wand toy or a bouncy spring, and the calm gives way to a lively chase, all pounces and skittering paws across the floor.

When the game winds down, they melt into whoever is holding them, easy to pick up and glad to be held. Watching the two of them tear around and then flop into a lap, it is clear these are kittens who feel completely at home.

[VIDEO — Mahi Mahi and Mackerel at play: editor to embed] Caption: Playtime

Bonded gray tabby kittens playing with toy | LoveMeow Credit: Orphan Kitten Project

Their gentle manners have won over everyone they meet. Neither one plays rough, and they do not scratch or bite, which makes them as easy to live with as they are to look at. They get along beautifully with other cats, too.

That easygoing streak runs deep. "They have also proven to be good with high-energy kids and high-energy yappy dogs," the rescue shared, the kind of pair who take a noisy, busy household in stride.

Taking it all in strideCredit: Orphan Kitten Project

New and startling things barely faze them either. Even the vacuum cleaner earns no more than a moment's pause before the two return to their contented selves.

The detail that truly wins people over, though, comes in the evenings. When the day slows down, Mahi Mahi and Mackerel like to stretch out along the high back of the couch, curled close together, keeping their foster company through a true crime documentary or two.

Come back hereCredit: Orphan Kitten Project

Lined up along the top of the cushions, calm and unbothered, they turn an ordinary night on the couch into their favorite part of the day.

It is a small, cozy ritual, and a long way from the crowded shelter where they started. Mahi Mahi and Mackerel are a bonded pair and will be adopted together.

Ready for a couch of their ownCredit: Orphan Kitten Project

Mahi Mahi and Mackerel started as two more kittens in a shelter with more animals than room. Now they are an easygoing pair with a favorite spot on the back of the couch, and a whole evening of documentaries waiting for the family who will watch along.

item.title: Two Cats Found Wary of the World and Alone on the Street Are Shy Apart, but Somehow a Team Together
item.description:
Two Tonkinese bonded cats were rescued from the streets and have spent years in foster care learning that people can be kind. Braver together than either could ever be alone, they form the best of teams side by side.

Jagger and JewellCredit: Best Friends Felines

Jagger and Jewell came into the care of Best Friends Felines after being found on the street, two frightened souls who had already learned to be wary of the world and the people in it. From the start, it was clear these two would ask for one thing in return for their trust, and that was time.

Best Friends Felines is a volunteer-run, no-kill cat rescue in south-east Queensland, Australia, one that keeps every cat it takes in with a foster family for as long as it takes to find the right home. Rather than rush the pair, their carers gave them exactly that, letting the two come around in their own time.

Slowly, day by day and year by year, the scared cats who first arrived began to soften, every small step forward met by carers who refused to give up on them. Through it all, the one constant has been each other.

Still a little unsureCredit: Best Friends Felines

When she feels settled, Jewell is the confident half of the pair. She greets her human every single morning, chatty and sweet, and will happily wander over for a gentle pat and a scratch.

She has even grown comfortable being brushed, sitting still while a person works the brush down her back, a kind of closeness she would have shied away from not long ago. "In time she may become a lap cat, but this will take a significant amount of time and patience," Judy of Best Friends Felines, the rescue caring for the pair, shared with LoveMeow.

Their favorite perchCredit: Best Friends Felines

Jagger is a big, handsome boy with a quieter, more timid heart. He is the shyer of the two, though his curiosity gives him away, and he loves to sit and watch his human move around the foster home.

He was a very good boy for the vet, calmly letting himself be lifted out of his carrier and weighed, and he grows a little braver by the day. "He is not at the stage where he will allow pats but is very curious about the goings-on in his current foster home," Judy shared.

Jagger, keeping watchCredit: Best Friends Felines

More than anything, Jagger and Jewell have each other. They are a truly bonded pair who must be adopted together, and their people would not have it any other way. "They take comfort from one another and rely on each other for confidence as they navigate the world around them," Judy shared.

That courage runs both ways. Watching them, it is easy to see how much braver each of them is with the other close by, one always steadying the other.

Never far apartCredit: Best Friends Felines

Their closeness shows most in the ordinary moments, the two of them moving through the day as a pair, one rarely more than a few feet away from the other.

They groom each other, share the best sleeping spots, and settle in wherever the other one already is. Apart, they are two shy cats. Together, they are a team.

Bonded Tonkinese cats greeting each other | LoveMeow Credit: Best Friends Felines

When their long-term foster could no longer keep them, the rescue began looking for someone willing to pick up where years of patient care left off. Both cats have thrived in quiet, calm surroundings, and Jagger in particular does best without the added unpredictability of dogs nearby.

Jagger and Jewell may not be the cats who march straight up and demand attention, but the people who know them understand just how special they are. With a little kindness and understanding, this pair has an enormous amount of love to give.

Braver togetherCredit: Best Friends Felines

Jagger and Jewell began as two frightened cats on the street, unsure of everyone around them. Years later, braver together than they ever were alone, they are ready for the one patient person who will finally call them home, together.

Share this story with your friends. Jagger and Jewell are in foster care with Best Friends Felines in south-east Queensland, Australia. You can view more on Instagram @bestfriendsfelines and Facebook.
